notes.md: - **Committee on External Affairs:** one of the **24 Departmentally Related Standing Committees**; serviced by the **Lok Sabha**; its Chairman is appointed by the **Speaker**; term **one year**. **Shashi Tharoor** was reappointed Chairman in the **2026** reconstitution.
- **First PM to visit Israel:** **Narendra Modi**, **4-6 July 2017**; it marked **25 years** of full diplomatic ties (set up in **1992** under Narasimha Rao).

new.s: Josip Broz Tito, one of the five founders of the Non-Aligned Movement, was the leader of which country?
new.x: Tito led Yugoslavia, which hosted the first NAM Summit at Belgrade in 1961.
new.angle: U0421 notes gap: Tito -> Yugoslavia (NAM founder)

new.s: Where was the 13th Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement held in 2003?
new.x: The 13th NAM Summit was held at Kuala Lumpur in 2003; Durban hosted the 12th (1998).
new.angle: U0421 notes gap: 13th NAM Summit -> Kuala Lumpur

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of the Cabinet Committee on Security?
new.x: The CCS is the PM with the Ministers of Finance, External Affairs, Home and Defence; Commerce is not a member.
new.angle: U0421 notes gap: CCS composition

new.s: Who was reappointed Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs in 2026?
new.x: In the 2026 reconstitution of the standing committees, Shashi Tharoor was reappointed Chairman of the Committee on External Affairs.
new.angle: U0421 web: PYQ yc9c40ea3ef9 parliamentary committee -> person heading it

new.s: Who appoints the Chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on External Affairs?
new.x: The Committee on External Affairs is serviced by the Lok Sabha, and its Chairman is appointed by the Speaker.
new.angle: U0421 web: PYQ yc9c40ea3ef9 committee -> head (appointing authority)

new.s: Who was the Prime Minister of India when the Pokhran-II nuclear tests were conducted in 1998?
new.x: Pokhran-II (Operation Shakti, 1998) was conducted under PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.
new.angle: U0422 notes gap: Pokhran-II -> Vajpayee

new.s: Under which Prime Minister did India conduct its first nuclear test at Pokhran in 1974?
new.x: Pokhran-I (18 May 1974), the 'peaceful nuclear explosion', was conducted under Indira Gandhi.
new.angle: U0422 notes gap: Pokhran-I -> Indira Gandhi

new.s: What was the code name of India's Pokhran-II nuclear tests of 1998?
new.x: The 1998 Pokhran-II tests were called Operation Shakti, after which India declared itself a nuclear-weapon state.
new.angle: U0422 notes gap: Pokhran-II code name -> Operation Shakti

new.s: In which year did an Indian Prime Minister visit Israel for the first time?
new.x: Narendra Modi made the first visit to Israel by an Indian Prime Minister in July 2017.
new.angle: U0422 web: PYQ y84e9f278e69 first PM to visit Israel

new.s: The first visit to Israel by an Indian Prime Minister, in July 2017, marked how many years of full diplomatic relations between the two countries?
new.x: India and Israel set up full diplomatic relations in 1992, so Modi's July 2017 visit marked 25 years.
new.angle: U0422 web: PYQ y84e9f278e69 PM -> Israel milestone

new.s: Under Article IX of the Indus Waters Treaty, to which body are 'disputes' referred?
new.x: Questions go to the Permanent Indus Commission, differences to a Neutral Expert and disputes to a Court of Arbitration.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: IWT disputes -> Court of Arbitration

new.s: Which terrorist group carried out the Pulwama attack on a CRPF convoy on 14 February 2019?
new.x: The Pulwama attack was carried out by Jaish-e-Mohammed; India responded with the Balakot airstrike.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: Pulwama -> JeM

new.s: In which district of Pakistan is Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur, located?
new.x: The Kartarpur Corridor links Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur) with Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur, in Narowal district.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: Kartarpur -> Narowal

new.s: Where did Lal Bahadur Shastri die in January 1966, soon after signing a declaration with Ayub Khan?
new.x: Shastri died at Tashkent just after signing the Tashkent Declaration with Ayub Khan.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: Shastri died at Tashkent

new.s: On which date did the Constitution of Jammu and Kashmir come into force?
new.x: The J&K Constituent Assembly approved accession on 17 November 1956 and the State's Constitution came into force on 26 January 1957.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: J&K Constitution in force -> 26 January 1957

new.s: On which date did the UN-arranged ceasefire end the first India-Pakistan war over Kashmir?
new.x: The 1947-48 war ended with the UN ceasefire of 1 January 1949; the Karachi Agreement of July 1949 then fixed the ceasefire line.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: first Kashmir war ceasefire -> 1 January 1949

new.s: In which year was the Samjhauta Express between India and Pakistan bombed?
new.x: The Samjhauta Express (Attari-Lahore) was bombed in 2007.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: Samjhauta Express bombing 2007

new.s: For how many years was the India-Pakistan agreement on the Kartarpur Corridor renewed in October 2024?
new.x: The Kartarpur Corridor agreement was renewed for 5 years in October 2024.
new.angle: U0423 notes gap: Kartarpur agreement renewal 2024

new.s: By what name does China refer to Arunachal Pradesh in its territorial claim?
new.x: China claims about 90,000 sq km in the north-east, most of Arunachal Pradesh, which it calls 'South Tibet'.
new.angle: U0424 notes gap: Arunachal -> 'South Tibet'

new.s: When did the India-China standoff at Sumdorong Chu in Tawang take place?
new.x: The Sumdorong Chu standoff in Tawang took place in 1986-87.
new.angle: U0424 notes gap: Sumdorong Chu -> 1986-87

new.s: To which party did Pushpa Kamal Dahal 'Prachanda', the first Prime Minister of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal, belong?
new.x: Prachanda of the UCPN (Maoist) became the first PM of the Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: first PM of Republic of Nepal -> Prachanda (UCPN-Maoist)

new.s: What is the capacity of the India-assisted Mangdechhu hydroelectric project in Bhutan?
new.x: Mangdechhu in Bhutan is a 720 MW project, inaugurated by the PM in 2019.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: Mangdechhu -> 720 MW

new.s: In which year was the India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement originally signed?
new.x: The Land Boundary Agreement was signed in 1974 and implemented in 2015 by the 100th Amendment.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: LBA signed 1974

new.s: The Indo-Sri Lanka Accord of 1987 provided for the merger of which provinces of Sri Lanka?
new.x: The 1987 Accord (Rajiv Gandhi-Jayewardene) provided for merging the Northern and Eastern provinces and devolution under the 13th Amendment.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: Indo-Sri Lanka Accord -> Northern and Eastern merger

new.s: Which LTTE chief was killed when the Sri Lankan Army crushed the LTTE in 2009?
new.x: In 2009 the Sri Lankan Army defeated the LTTE and its chief V. Prabhakaran was killed.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: LTTE chief killed 2009 -> Prabhakaran

new.s: With which organisation did India restore the Stor Palace in Kabul, completed in 2016?
new.x: The Stor Palace in Kabul was restored by India with the Aga Khan Trust for Culture and completed in 2016.
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: Stor Palace -> Aga Khan Trust for Culture

new.s: With which neighbour does India share its second-longest land border?
new.x: Bangladesh (4,096.7 km) is first and China (3,488 km) second, ahead of Pakistan (3,323 km).
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: border lengths -> China second-longest

new.s: With which country is the Rohingya refugee issue chiefly linked?
new.x: The Rohingya issue concerns Myanmar (and Bangladesh, where many have fled).
new.angle: U0425 notes gap: Rohingya -> Myanmar

new.s: What is the full form of MAHASAGAR, India's upgraded maritime vision of 2025?
o: Maritime Alliance for Harmony and Security Across Global and Asian Regions
Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions
Multilateral Holistic Approach to Security and Growth in the Asian Region
Mutual Help and Security Agreement for Growth and Regional Advancement
new.x: MAHASAGAR, announced in Mauritius in 2025, means Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: MAHASAGAR full form

new.s: What is the full form of SHANTI, India's framework for shared maritime spaces announced in July 2026?
o: Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity
Security and Harmony Among Nations Through Integration
Shared Harbours and Navigation Through Indian Ocean
Strategic Harmony and Norms for Trade in the Indo-Pacific
new.x: SHANTI, announced by EAM Jaishankar on 13 July 2026, stands for Securing Holistic Advancement through Norms, Trust and Integrity.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: SHANTI full form

new.s: Besides the Central Asian states, which country was invited to the first India-Central Asia Dialogue at Samarkand in 2019?
new.x: The first India-Central Asia Dialogue of foreign ministers (Samarkand, 2019) also invited Afghanistan.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: 1st India-Central Asia Dialogue -> Afghanistan invited

new.s: In which year did India and Vietnam raise their ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership?
new.x: Under Act East, India-Vietnam ties became a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in 2016.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: Vietnam CSP 2016

new.s: Which ASEAN country became India's strategic partner in August 2025?
new.x: India and the Philippines became strategic partners in August 2025; Malaysia's ties became a CSP in 2024.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: Philippines strategic partner 2025

new.s: Which grouping is India's largest socio-economic partner in West Asia, with trade of over $160 billion?
new.x: The GCC is India's largest socio-economic partner in the region, with over $160 billion trade and about 10 million Indians.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: GCC largest partner

new.s: Which service hosts the Information Fusion Centre-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) at Gurugram?
new.x: The IFC-IOR, inaugurated on 22 December 2018 at IMAC, Gurugram, is hosted by the Indian Navy.
new.angle: U0426 notes gap: IFC-IOR host -> Indian Navy
